Its chapters discuss the struggles and circumstances of Imam Ali, Imam al-Hasan, Imam Zayn al-Abidin, Imam al-Sadiq, Imam al-Kazim, Imam al-Rida and Imam al-Hasan al-Askari, and end with the promised Mahdi and universal justice.
sample_questions: What were the lives of the twelve Imams like?
Why did Imam al-Hasan make peace?
Why was Imam al-Kazim killed?
What was Imam al-Rida's role as crown prince?
Who is the promised Mahdi?

records.title: Tasawwuf the Meeting Point of Tashayyu and Tasannun
records.description: An article in the Al-Tawhid journal. The site's summary says it presents Sufism (tasawwuf, Islamic mysticism) as a meeting point of the Shia and Sunni schools and as a sign pointing towards unity between them.
sample_questions: What is Sufism?
Is Sufism a meeting point of Shia and Sunni Islam?
What is tasawwuf?
How can Shias and Sunnis find common ground?

records.title: Tawhid, The Unity of God from the Holy Qur'an
records.description: A booklet that collects verses from the Quran on Tawhid, the unity or oneness of God, arranged by surah, with a short introduction to the Quran. It is published by the World Organization for Islamic Services.
sample_questions: What does the Quran say about the oneness of God?
What is Tawhid?
Which Quran verses talk about God's unity?
What does Surah al-Ikhlas say?

records.title: Tears For Karbala
records.description: A book that, the site says, presents children with traditional majalis (gatherings with lectures) for the twelve days of Muharram. Its twelve majlis chapters cover the arrival at Karbala, the companions and family members of Imam Husayn, and the Imam himself.
sample_questions: What happens in a Muharram majlis?
Who were the companions of Imam Husayn at Karbala?
Is there a Karbala book for children?
Who was Hazrat Abbas?
Who was Ali Asghar?

records.title: Tenets of Islam
records.description: Short passages by Shaykh Tusi on the main Islamic beliefs: the attributes of God, monotheism, justice, the grace of God, prophethood, infallibility, the Seal of the Prophets, and related topics. Each chapter is brief and covers one belief.
sample_questions: What are the attributes of God in Islam?
What is monotheism, or tawhid?
What is the meaning of divine justice?
What does 'Seal of the Prophets' mean?

records.title: The Ahlul Bayt
records.description: A short article (about 1,200 words) that begins by saying the Ahlul Bayt are the Godly ones of the Prophet's family. Its sections cite Qur'anic themes such as knowledge, purity, love for the family, and acknowledgement of Ali as successor.
sample_questions: Who are the Ahlul Bayt?
Why do Shias love the Ahlul Bayt?
What does the Quran say about the Ahlul Bayt?
Who is the Prophet's family in Shia Islam?

records.title: The Koran
records.description: The introduction to the book Vision of Islam (Paragon House, 1994), about the Koran (Qur'an) and what it means to Muslims as revelation. It is an excerpt of about 2,400 words presented on the site as an article.
sample_questions: What is the Quran?
Why is the Quran central for Muslims?
How do Muslims view revelation?
What is the Koran?

records.title: The Last Luminary
records.description: A short book on the history of the Shia belief in Imam al-Mahdi, the twelfth Imam, covering the good news of his coming, his birth, the minor and major occultation (his period of hiddenness), and the Shia during the occultation.
sample_questions: Who is Imam al-Mahdi?
What is the occultation?
What is the minor occultation?
What do Shias believe about the twelfth Imam?
Where can I read a brief history of the Mahdi belief?

records.title: The Prayer of a Mother
records.description: A very short story (roughly 350-400 words), an excerpt from the book When Faith Reigns, that begins with a stranger and traveller arriving at a door. The site tags it Mother, Salah (Prayers) and Young Muslim.
sample_questions: Are there short Islamic stories for young Muslims?
What is a story about a mother's prayer?
Where can I find stories about prayer for children?
What can children learn from a mother's prayer?

records.title: Some Thoughts on the Road to Islamic Solidarity
records.description: A journal article from Al-Taqrib that calls for Muslims to become more familiar with and accepting of one another. It looks at education, travel, the Hajj pilgrimage, the Arabic language, and political and economic steps towards solidarity.
sample_questions: How can Muslims become more united?
What role does Hajj play in Muslim unity?
How can education bring Muslims together?
What is Islamic solidarity?
Why does the Arabic language matter for unity?

records.title: Treatise On Rights (Risalat al-Huquq)
records.description: The only longer work attributed to Imam Ali Zayn al-Abidin besides his supplications and short sayings. It lists the rights that God, the self, bodily organs, acts of worship and other people have, as an elaboration of a well-known saying of the Prophet.
sample_questions: What are the rights in Islam according to Imam Zayn al-Abidin?
What is Risalat al-Huquq?
What is the right of the tongue?
What did the fourth Imam teach about human rights?

records.title: The Twelve Successors of the Holy Prophet
records.description: A book on the Prophet's narrations about the number of his successors and the twelve Imams. It examines those narrations and their explanations, presents the twelve Imams as the school of the caliphate records them, and ends with a brief account of each successor.
sample_questions: How many successors did the Prophet Muhammad name?
Who are the twelve Imams in Shia belief?
What do the narrations about the twelve successors say?
What is the Imamate?

records.title: Types of Unity in the Qur’an and Fundamental Causes of Disunity
records.description: A translated journal article on the kinds of unity the Qur'an speaks of (the Muslim community, followers of earlier scriptures, all religions, humanity) and on causes of disunity, which it lists as politics, differences of school (madhhab) and ethnicity.
sample_questions: What does the Qur'an say about unity?
What causes disunity among Muslims?
What are the types of unity?
Why are there different schools of thought in Islam?
How can Muslims unite?

records.title: Understanding God's Mercy Part 2
records.description: A journal paper, part 2 of 8, on God's mercy and His purpose in creating humans, drawing on the Qur'an, divine sayings and the prayers and hadiths of the Ahl al-Bayt. Sections cover God's names such as al-Rahman and al-Rahim.
sample_questions: What is God's mercy in Islam?
What does al-Rahman al-Rahim mean?
Why did God create humans?
What are the names of God?

records.title: Understanding the Month of Glory Lessons on the Month of Ramadhan
records.description: A book of lessons and activities about the month of Ramadan, which the site describes as being for children and youth. Chapters include Quran verses and sayings on fasting, an Imam's welcome to the month, a Ramadan checklist, reasons Muslims fast, and thoughts on Eid.
sample_questions: What is the month of Ramadan about?
Why do Muslims fast in Ramadan?
What is Eid?
Is there a Ramadan activity book for kids?
What should I do during Ramadan?

records.title: The Uprising of Ashura and Responses to Doubts
records.description: A detailed book on Imam Husayn's life and character and the tragedy of Karbala, according to the site. It also covers Shia mourning practices such as crying and reciting elegies, and answers questions about the uprising, such as who killed Imam Husayn.
sample_questions: Who was Imam Husayn?
What happened on Ashura?
Why do Shias mourn and cry for Imam Husayn?
Who killed Imam Husayn?
Why did Imam Husayn take his family to Karbala?
What is the meaning of Muharram?

records.title: Various Sayings of Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib (as)
records.description: A compilation of sayings of Imam Ali, with extracts from Du'a Kumayl and from Nahj al-Balagha. Topics include knowledge, intellect, faith, the heart and the illusion of this world, and it includes two sermons written without dots and without the letter alif. The site tags it 'Youth' and 'Short Sayings'.
sample_questions: What are famous sayings of Imam Ali?
What did Imam Ali say about knowledge?
What did Imam Ali say about the intellect?
What is the sermon without dots?
What did Imam Ali say about this world?

records.title: Was Muhammad (S) a Prophet of Terror?!
records.description: An article that examines certain historical reports about killings in the time of the Prophet, answering the question in its title. Its sections give examples, analyse the reports and discuss who the real victims of terrorism are.
sample_questions: Was Prophet Muhammad a terrorist?
Did the Prophet order assassinations?
What does Islam say about terrorism?
How should historical reports about the Prophet be analysed?

records.title: What Does It Mean To Be A Muslim?
records.description: A short article (about 850 to 900 words) that looks at what being a Muslim means. It sets out four points, covering the legal definition of a Muslim, belonging to the Muslim community, holding the values and doctrines taught in Islam, and behaving in line with them.
sample_questions: What does it mean to be a Muslim?
Who counts as a Muslim?
What do Muslims believe?
Is being Muslim about belief or about behaviour?
How do you belong to the Muslim community?

records.title: What Everyone Should Know about Islam
records.description: A summary of the principles of religion by Ayatollah Ibrahim Amini, written for general readers. Its chapters cover theology, prophethood, the Imamate, the Resurrection, moral ethics and the branches of religion. The book presents itself as a summary that points readers to fuller works.
sample_questions: What are the principles of religion in Islam?
What is prophethood in Islam?
What is the Imamate?
What happens after death in Islam?
What does Islam teach about ethics?

records.title: What is 'Ashoora?
records.description: A short article about Ashura, the tenth day of Muharram, when Shias remember the killing of Imam Husayn at Karbala. Its two sections ask what led to the events of Karbala and what the purpose of Imam Husayn's sacrifice was.
sample_questions: What is Ashura?
Why do Shias mourn in Muharram?
What led to the tragedy of Karbala?
Why did Imam Husayn sacrifice his life?
What is the purpose of Ashura?
What happened on the tenth of Muharram?

records.title: What A Muslim Should Know And Believe
records.description: A short booklet that the site calls brief and simple, explaining the main articles of faith: Tawhid (the oneness of God), divine justice, prophethood, the Imamate and the Day of Judgement. It also explains some terms and lists major sins. The site says it is a guide for parents whose children are reaching maturity.
sample_questions: What are the main beliefs of a Shia Muslim?
What are the roots of religion (Usul al-Deen)?
What does Shia mean?
What are major sins?
What should a young Muslim know about belief?

records.title: Personalities: What Non-Muslims Say About 'Ali, The First Successor of Prophet Muhammad
records.description: A short collection of brief quotations about Imam Ali from notable people of other faiths, including Thomas Carlyle, Edward Gibbon and Wilferd Madelung. The page credits the Ahlul Bayt Digital Islamic Library Project as compiler.
sample_questions: What do non-Muslims say about Imam Ali?
Who was Imam Ali?
What did Thomas Carlyle say about Ali?
What do historians think of Imam Ali?

records.title: When Power and Piety Collide
records.description: A study of early Islamic history and the caliphate, looking at the first three caliphs, the Quraysh, the Saqifah gathering, and the early handling of hadith. First U.S. edition 2009, Islamic Educational Center of Orange County.
sample_questions: What happened at Saqifah?
Who were the first three caliphs?
How did early Muslim politics affect hadith?
Why did the Muslim community split?

records.title: Yazid son of Mu‘awiyah and his son, Historical Stories For Children 2
records.description: Second book in a 'Historical Stories For Children' series. The site says it looks at the character of Yazid, son of Mu'awiyah, and it includes a chapter on his son, the second Mu'awiyah.
sample_questions: Who was Yazid?
Who was Yazid's son?
Is there a history book for children about the Umayyad rulers?
Why is Yazid important in Shia history?

records.title: Imam Ali Ibn al Husayn (as)
records.description: An account of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), the fourth Imam of the Twelver Shia, taken from a classical work credited on the page to al-Mufid. It opens with his birth and goes on to a brief survey of reports about him.
sample_questions: Who was Imam Zayn al-Abidin?
Who was the fourth Imam of the Shia?
When was Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn born?
What do early sources report about Imam Zayn al-Abidin?
Who was the son of Imam Husayn who survived Karbala?

records.title: Ziyaarat Aale-Yaasin, A Brief Commentary
records.description: A brief verse-by-verse explanation of Ziyaarat Aale-Yaasin, a salutation attributed to Imam al-Mahdi, with the Arabic text and a note on its chain of narrators. Published by the Association of Imam Mahdi in Shaabaan 1425 A.H.
sample_questions: What is Ziyaarat Aale-Yaasin?
What does Ziyarat Al Yasin mean?
Who narrated the Ziyarat of Imam Mahdi?
Is there a commentary on Ziyarat Aale Yaseen?

records.title: A Code of Practice For Muslims in the West
records.description: A book of practical Islamic rulings (fiqh) written for Muslims living in non-Muslim countries, following the views of Sayyid Ali al-Sistani. Each chapter has a short introduction, general rules, and questions and answers, on topics such as prayer, fasting, food, work, marriage and medical issues.
sample_questions: How do I practise Islam while living in the West?
Is there a book of Islamic rules for Muslims in non-Muslim countries?
Where can I read Ayatollah Sistani's rulings for Muslims in the West?
What does Islam say about everyday life in a non-Muslim country?
Where do I find Shia rulings on food, work and marriage in the West?

records.title: Obligation to perform Hajj
records.description: The opening page of the book, on the duty of Hajj in Islam: its place among the basic principles of faith, the idea of Hajjatul Islam (the first obligatory Hajj), and the arrangements for the journey.
sample_questions: Is Hajj compulsory?
What is Hajjatul Islam?
How often does a Muslim perform Hajj?
Why is Hajj important in Islam?

records.title: Conditions which make Hajjatul Islam obligatory
records.description: Covers the conditions that bring Hajjatul Islam (the first obligatory Hajj) into effect, and how financial ability is judged, including cases of loans and gifts.
sample_questions: Who has to perform Hajj?
What does having the means for Hajj mean?
Does a child's Hajj count as the first obligatory Hajj?
What if I have to borrow money for Hajj?
What does having sound mind have to do with Hajj?

records.title: Making a will regarding pilgrimage
records.description: Rules on making a will regarding pilgrimage: what a person on their deathbed owes, how a Hajj is arranged after death, and how it is paid for from the estate.
sample_questions: Can I leave a will for Hajj to be done for me?
What if someone died without performing Hajj?
How is Hajj paid for after a person's death?
Who arranges a pilgrimage left in a will?

records.title: The rules on pilgrimage by proxy (Niyabah)
records.description: Rules on pilgrimage by proxy (niyabah), where one person performs Hajj for another. Covers the qualifications of the person acting as agent and how the arrangement is made.
sample_questions: Can someone perform Hajj on my behalf?
What is niyabah?
Who can perform Hajj for another person?
What are the conditions for an agent in Hajj?

records.title: Various kinds of Umrah
records.description: Describes the kinds of Umrah (the lesser pilgrimage) and how each relates to Hajj, including when Umrah itself is a duty and which type fits which situation.
sample_questions: What is Umrah?
What are the types of Umrah?
Is Umrah obligatory?
What is the difference between Umrah and Hajj?

records.title: Optional pilgrimage
records.description: Short page on optional (recommended) pilgrimage: Hajj or Umrah done beyond the obligatory one, and recommended practices at departure and in sending others on pilgrimage.
sample_questions: Can I perform Hajj more than once?
What is recommended Hajj?
Can I send someone else on pilgrimage?
What is recommended when leaving Mecca?

records.title: Types of Hajj
records.description: Introduces the three types of Hajj (Tamatu', Ifraad and Qiraan) and which type applies to people living far from or near Mecca.
sample_questions: What are the types of Hajj?
What is Hajj Tamatu'?
Which type of Hajj applies to someone living far from Mecca?
What is the difference between Ifraad and Qiraan?

records.title: Hajj-ut-Tamatu
records.description: Covers Hajj-ut-Tamatu', made up of Umrah followed by Hajj, and lists the actions involved in the Umrah part, such as ihram, tawaf, prayer, sa'y and taqseer.
sample_questions: What is Hajj Tamatu'?
What are the steps of Umrat-ut-Tamatu'?
What comes first, Umrah or Hajj?
What is the order of acts in Hajj Tamatu'?

records.title: Hajj-ul-Ifraad
records.description: Covers Hajj-ul-Ifraad, a distinct kind of pilgrimage for people living in or near Mecca, and how it relates to Umrah done separately.
sample_questions: What is Hajj Ifraad?
Who performs Hajj Ifraad?
How is Ifraad different from Tamatu'?
Is a separate Umrah done with Ifraad?

records.title: Meqats for wearing ihram
records.description: Covers the Meqats, the designated places where a pilgrim puts on ihram (the state of pilgrim dress and restrictions). Lists the nine places and who each is for, including questions on arriving by air.

Where do pilgrims enter ihram?
Where do people from Medina enter ihram?
How do I enter ihram if I fly to Jeddah?

records.title: Ihram procedure
records.description: Covers the procedure for entering ihram: the intention (niyyah), the talbiyah (the pilgrim's recited call), and the required garments for men and women.
sample_questions: How do I enter ihram?
What is talbiyah?
What do I wear in ihram?
What is the intention for Hajj?
What are the obligations of ihram?

records.title: Prohibitions during Ihram
records.description: Lists the acts a pilgrim avoids once in ihram, such as hunting, perfume, certain clothing, covering the head, cutting hair and certain personal conduct, and what is owed if one of them is done.
sample_questions: What is forbidden in ihram?
Can I use perfume in ihram?
What are the penalties for breaking ihram rules?
Can I wear a ring or watch in ihram?
What clothing do men avoid in ihram?

records.title: Matters forbidden within (The Haram)
records.description: Covers the matters restricted within the Haram (the sacred area around Mecca), such as hunting and cutting plants, and who these restrictions cover.

What is not allowed within the Haram?

records.title: Boundaries of Haram
records.description: Describes the boundaries of the Haram around Mecca and of Medina, as handed down, and where each boundary lies.

How far does the Haram of Mecca extend?

records.title: Tawaf
records.description: Introduces tawaf (circling the Kaaba) as part of Umrat-ut-Tamatu', and covers delay, the intention, and the conditions for performing it.

records.title: Obligations of Tawaf
records.description: Lists the eight obligations of tawaf, including where to start and finish, the direction, the number of rounds and staying within the prescribed area.
sample_questions: Where does tawaf begin?
What are the obligations of tawaf?
How many circuits make a tawaf?

records.description: Covers situations where a person steps outside the bounds of tawaf, such as entering the Kaaba or the Shadharwaan, and how this affects the tawaf.

What if I enter the Kaaba during tawaf?

records.title: Irregularities in Tawaf
records.description: Covers irregularities in tawaf, including interrupting it, stopping partway, doubts about the number of rounds and what to do next.

records.title: Tawaf prayer
records.description: Covers the two-raka'a prayer performed after tawaf: how it is said, where it is performed near Maqam Ibrahim, and related questions.

records.title: Obligations of Sa'y
records.description: Covers the obligations of sa'y (walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah): intention, where it starts and ends, and the number of trips.

records.title: Taqseer
records.description: Covers taqseer (cutting a small amount of hair or nails) that ends the Umrah, including what counts as taqseer and what it releases the pilgrim from.

records.title: Ihram for Hajj
records.description: Covers putting on ihram for the Hajj itself: the best time, the place, and the thirteen obligations of Hajj in outline.

records.title: Wuquf at Arafat
records.description: Covers wuquf at Arafat (the standing and staying at the plain of Arafat), the second obligation of Hajj-ut-Tamatu': intention, the time and place, and related rules.

records.title: Shaving the head and Taqseer

records.description: Covers tawaf-un-nisa and the prayer that follows it, the tenth and eleventh obligations of Hajj, and how they differ from the essential parts of Hajj.

records.title: Persons prevented from performing Hajj
records.description: Covers pilgrims who are prevented from performing Hajj, either after entering ihram (blocked or turned away) or otherwise, and the rules on what follows.

records.title: Al-Amālī: The Dictations
records.description: A transcription of 42 assemblies in which Shaykh al-Mufid dictated narrations to his students, shown with an English translation by Mulla Asgharali M M Jaffer. The site says it holds 387 narrations attributed to the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt (the Prophet's family) on historical, ethical and doctrinal topics. Its assemblies cover topics such as the recording of good deeds, the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt, supplications at dawn and dusk, the great sins, Ramadan and the fear of Allah. It is a primary source for readers with some background.

records.title: Al-Imāma wa’l-Tabṣira min al-Ḥayra: Divine Leadership & Insight amidst Confusion
records.description: An early hadith collection (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) on divine leadership (the Imamate) compiled by 'Ali ibn Babawayh, the father of Shaykh al-Saduq according to the site, shown with an English translation by Haseeb Hassan. records.title: Al-Tawḥīd: The Book of Divine Unity
records.description: A collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) about God, compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq and translated into English by Sayed Ali Raza Rizvi. It is a primary source for readers who want the narrations behind Shia beliefs about God.

records.title: Kamāl al-Dīn wa Tamām al-Niʿma: The Perfection of the Religion

The second section, 'The Occultations and the Proofs', begins with accounts of earlier prophets who were hidden for periods, such as Idris and Yusuf. It is a primary source for readers with some background.

The site says it is organised alphabetically and is also known as 'Rijal Ibn al-Ghada'iri' (rijal means the study of narrators). Its chapters are grouped by the first letter of each narrator's name, from Alif to Ya, with one chapter on kunyas (names that begin with Abu) and an addendum of material quoted from other authors. It is not a hadith collection; it is a tool for studying who transmitted hadith.
